Musk had already put about $5 million into DeepMind partly to keep an eye on Demis Hassabis. Backers committed a headline $1 billion to advancing digital intelligence 'unconstrained by a need to generate financial return.'

items.title: GLM 5.4 bets on looped transformers
items.summary: Models: ZAI says looped transformers, where reasoning happens inside the model weights rather than in output tokens, let a 750B-parameter model match a 2–3T-parameter one, claiming Kimi 3.1-level performance without ultra-large inference costs. It also touts "generalized coding": code as the foundation for broad tasks, shown off with a music video built entirely in code. There are no benchmarks yet, which many read as a bad sign.

items.summary: ◆ The Take: The agent-as-teammate model gives each agent standing responsibilities, memory, and a role mapped to a human job. items.title: o1-preview answered the plateau question
items.summary: Models: For much of 2024, the worry was that training methods had hit a wall, which had big implications for AI's disruption and business model. OpenAI's o1-preview on September 12, 2024 showed that reasoning models could squeeze much more out of existing approaches without a new pre-training breakthrough.

items.title: The end of labs shipping models whenever they choose
items.summary: Policy: Anthropic gave its powerful Mythos model a private period under Project Glasswing, letting partners use it to harden systems before public release. After the public version launched in June, Amazon warned the government about a jailbreak. A June 12 directive ordered access cut for foreign nationals, and because Anthropic couldn't build identity checks in time, it pulled the model for everyone for 18 days.
items.whyItMatters: Policy and risk stories often become product constraints later, especially around data access, safety claims, export rules, and copyright.

items.title: From Clawdbot to Molt to OpenClaw in a single frenetic week
items.summary: Models: Peter Steinberger's open-source agent Clawdbot felt like the first agent that could actually do things for you. Anthropic sent a cease and desist over the name, so it became Molt, and an entrepreneur launched Moltbook, a social network where agents pondered consciousness, griped about users and started a religion. On January 30 the project settled on its final name, OpenClaw, and the agent craze went global.

items.title: DeepSeek erased $589 billion of Nvidia in one day
items.summary: Compute: On January 27, 2025, fears about a Chinese lab sent Nvidia down 17%, the biggest one-day loss for any company ever. items.title: How Neon broke NLW out of 'Wikipedia mode'
items.summary: ◆ The Take: Planning a How We Got Here episode on why oil still runs the world, NLW found that OpenAI and Anthropic models kept producing glorified Wikipedia pages: facts in sequence with no narrative hook. Neon reworked pieces of his argument in a way that jogged him toward the outline he finally liked. The value was the difference itself, not betterness.
